accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement for Your Support
accessibility.section0:
This accessibility statement applies to the Your Support service.

This website is run by HM Courts and Tribunals Service. We want as many people as possible to be able to use this website. For example, that means you should be able to:

  • change colours, contrast levels and fonts using browser or device settings
  • zoom in up to 400% without the text spilling off the screen
  • navigate most of the website using a keyboard or speech recognition software
  • listen to most of the website using a screen reader (including the most recent versions of JAWS, NVDA and VoiceOver)

We’ve also made the website text as simple as possible to understand.

AbilityNet has advice on making your device easier to use if you have a disability.
accessibility.section1:
How accessible the Your Support service is

We know some parts of this service are not fully accessible. For example:

  • the sign out link is implemented as a landmark, which means navigation may not be as expected
accessibility.section2:
Feedback and contact information

We’re always looking to improve the accessibility of this service. If you find any accessibility problems not listed on this page or think we are not meeting accessibility requirements, contact: cui-team@HMCTS.NET

Contact the service dealing with your case if you need to:

  • tell us about your support needs
  • ask for an update on a support request
  • ask for information in a different text, audio or other format

accessibility.section4:
Enforcement procedure

The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) is responsible for enforcing the Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility Regulations 2018 (the ‘accessibility regulations’). If you’re not happy with how we respond to your complaint, contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service (EASS).
accessibility.section5:
Technical information about this online form’s accessibility

We are committed to making this form accessible, in accordance with the Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility Regulations 2018.
accessibility.section6:
Compliance status

This website is fully compliant with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines version 2.2 AA standard.

This service is partially compliant with the standard, due to the non‑compliances listed below.
accessibility.section7:
Non-accessible content

The content listed below is non-accessible for the following reasons:

Non-compliance with the accessibility regulations

The sign out link is implemented as a landmark. Users that rely on screen readers may face confusion as they may not expect to land on a sign out link when navigating the page using landmark menu shortcuts. Fails WCAG 2.4.4: (Link Purpose (In Context)) and WCAG 4.1.2: (Name, Role, Value)
accessibility.section8:
What we’re doing to improve accessibility

This website is continually tested using accessibility automated tests and basic manual and assistive technology checks. Any new features which are introduced will also be tested internally or with the support of the internal HMCTS accessibility testing team.

The sign out link will be reviewed with the GOV.UK branding, which includes other design changes. Read more information about these changes to GOV.UK
accessibility.section9:
Preparation of this accessibility statement

This statement was prepared on 17th Sep 2025. It was last reviewed on 29th July 2026.

This website was last tested on 21 April 2025 against the WCAG 2.2 AA standard.

The audit was carried out by the internal HMCTS accessibility testing team. The team tested against a range of assistive technologies and accessibility testing tools.

The statement will be reviewed for accuracy at least once a year.
